title: On Making $\mathrm{SE}(2)$-Invariant Networks Optimal
abstract: arXiv:2610.17424v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Respecting a-priori known symmetries of underlying data is a key principle in designing efficient neural architectures. Convolutional neural networks are a canonical example, encoding translation equivariance. Extending this inductive bias to richer symmetry groups such as $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ in the most effective way possible is an ongoing architectural and computational challenge. Building on classical invariant theory, we derive invariant feature maps that are provably optimal: minimal and information-preserving with respect to the symmetry group. Our construction is designed to integrate seamlessly into standard architectures, requiring no modification to nonlinearities or normalization layers. As a concrete implementation, we introduce a plug-and-play module for convolutional neural networks that enforces $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ invariance, capturing both translations and rotations within standard architectures. tldr: 该论文基于经典不变理论推导出可证明最优（既最小又信息保持）的 SE(2) 不变特征映射，并提出一个即插即用模块，使标准卷积神经网络无需修改架构即可同时捕获平移与旋转不变性。
en_tdlr: Building on classical invariant theory, this paper derives provably optimal (minimal and information-preserving) SE(2)-invariant feature maps and introduces a plug-and-play module that enables standard CNNs to capture both translations and rotations without any architectural modifications.
